newsitem.title: INDIA: Lehman sees India 97/98 growth at about seven pct.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees India 97/98 growth at about seven pct.

text.p: Global investment bank Lehman Brothers expects India to achieve annual economic growth of about seven percent, its Asia chief said on Monday.

"I think we are talking about something in the seven percent range which is a bit less than what I have heard from some others," C. Daniel Tyree, chairman of Lehman Brothers Asia, told Reuters television when asked for his forecast for India's 1997/98 (April-March) fiscal year.
"But (seven percent is) still very significant when compared to what's going on in Europe, the US and other parts of Asia. That's a very positive number," Tyree said.

India expects its gross domestic product (GDP) to grow at a real rate of seven percent or more in the fiscal year starting on April 1, Finance Ministry officials said on Saturday. The economy is forecast to post GDP growth of 6.8 percent in 1996/97.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's 1997/98 federal budget was "a big step in the right direction," Tyree said. "We are very positive about what the Finance Minister and the government have said on Friday," he added.
Chidambaram on Friday cut corporate and income taxes and slashed import tariffs in the budget for 1997/98.
